Thanks Diane — solid ask. Attached is a focused MAP (v2) that lays out the evaluation plan, decision gates, and a recommended path for deployment mode + region. Summary here so it's easy to consume: 

Summary recommendation (short):
- PoC: Hosted (fastest onboarding, no infra commit) scoped to US-East for latency tests and integration verification.
- Production (GA): Dedicated Reserved Capacity in US-East (predictable latency & throughput, supports autoscale/burst).
- Blocked/Risk scenario: Private (on-prem/VPC) as a compliance fallback for the regulated division; can be staged if legal requires additional controls (HSM/KMS integration).

Proposed timeline (high level):
- Week 1 (2026-04-19): Kickoff + PoC config on Hosted (sample traffic, KV cache warm-up).
- Weeks 2–4 (2026-04-26 to 2026-05-16): Performance and regression evals; iterate prompts/config.
- Week 5 (2026-05-17): Decision gate — Hosted->Dedicated schedule if metrics meet latency & cost SLOs.
- Weeks 6–10 (2026-05-18 to 2026-06-25): Dedicated capacity provisioning + final acceptance; target GA 2026-06-15 (conservative buffer allocated).

Key technical notes / tradeoffs:
- Hosted lets us validate end-to-end quickly (no infra lead time).
- Dedicated reduces per-token cost at scale and gives predictable tail latencies; requires a 30–60 day provisioning window depending on SKU & region commitments.
- Private is the highest compliance bar (HSM, air-gapped options) but adds >8 weeks for infra + legal HLD.

Action items for Medsys (what we need from you):
1) Confirm the US-East region preference and any specific data residency SLA.
2) Provide the SOC2 questionnaire items (we will map them to evidence) — procurement attached a list, which we reviewed.
3) Confirm whether you want Redwood to provision Dedicated capacity on contract signature or only after acceptance testing.

I've attached medsys_MAP_v2.pdf (draft) and a short appendix with rough provisioning lead times. Karthik, Priyom — please add technical constraints or call-outs I missed.

Best,

Neha / Diane — quick technical addendum from infra: 

- Latency: US-East Dedicated gives median latency improvement ~12–18% vs generic Hosted in our benchmarks for similar token sizes when KV caching and batching are tuned. We should validate with your average sequence length and concurrency profile in PoC.
- Cost: Dedicated amortizes better at sustained throughput (we'll provide model-by-model tCO estimates once you share projected RPS).
- Provisioning: Dedicated SKUs in us-east-1 typically require 3–6 weeks for guaranteed reserved pools if we need specific GPU types; 6–8 weeks for capacity with HSM attachment.
- Fallbacks: We recommend a staged plan — start on Hosted, flip traffic to Dedicated behind a canary once pools are online. Private should be treated as a last-resort runway (legal-driven).

Operational asks for Medsys:
- Can you share a representative request log or sample traffic? (5–7 days of traffic is ideal).
- Any hard cutover blackout windows we should avoid in June?

I added inline comments in the MAP draft (see medsys_MAP_v2.pdf). Priyom — can you confirm SLO language we should include for the canary?

-Karthik
